    The key lemma on efficient tackles (BGRS 8.4) #

    If the last morphism t of an efficient hook tackle occurs in a path v of an essential contour (v, w), then t is the first arrow of v (RayCat.key_hook). The proof is BGRS's alternating induction down the tackle: at each stage a candidate tackle with larger efficiency is built from the first or last arrow of w; since it cannot be a tackle, a chain condition fails, and every failure either makes v and w interlaced or moves one step down. Left and right cancellation are assumed (they hold for the ray categories of distributive algebras). Fischbacher's variant (tackles ending in an arrow of an essential contour) is covered by the admissibility predicate.

            theorem LargeIndecomposable.RayCat.key_hook {P : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} P] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms P] [IsRayCategory P] {adm : RayMor P → Prop} {o : ℕ} {l : List (RayMor P)} {x y : RayVert P} {v w : Quiver.Path x y} (hL : LeftCancel P) (hR : RightCancel P) (hl : IsEfficient adm o l) (m : ℕ) (hm : m + 1 = l.length) (hev : (m + o) % 2 = 0) {yα yζ : RayVert P} (α : x ⟶ yα) (w₃ : Quiver.Path yα y) (hwα : w = α.toPath.comp w₃) (hadmα : adm ⟨x.out, ⟨yα.out, ↑α⟩⟩) (w₂ : Quiver.Path x yζ) (ζ : yζ ⟶ y) (hwζ : w = w₂.cons ζ) (hadmζ : adm ⟨yζ.out, ⟨y.out, ↑ζ⟩⟩) (hvw : pathVal v = pathVal w) (hv0 : pathVal v ≠ 0) (hni : ¬Interlaced v w) (X Z : P) (hX : l[m].fst = X) (hZ : l[m].snd.fst = Z) (p : Quiver.Path x (RayVert.mk X)) (r : Quiver.Path (RayVert.mk X) (RayVert.mk Z)) (u : Quiver.Path (RayVert.mk Z) y) (hr : pathVal r = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (CategoryTheory.eqToHom ⋯) (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp l[m].snd.snd (CategoryTheory.eqToHom hZ))) (hv : v = (p.comp r).comp u) :
            p.length = 0

            Key lemma (BGRS 8.4, hook case). Let l be an efficient tackle whose last link is a valley (m + o even), and (v, w) an essential contour whose first and last arrows are admissible. If v passes through a path r for l[m], then r starts at the beginning of v.
